details:
LunaNav is an interactive web-based decision-support prototype for exploring potential lunar south-pole landing sites. It uses published lunar illumination and Earth-visibility data to help users compare candidate sites under different mission objectives.

Users can select a mission goal such as Solar Power, Earth Communication, Scientific Research, or Multiple Goals. They can apply different priority weights, compare candidate sites, review modeled sunlight and Sun+Earth visibility, set minimum sunlight requirements, and identify the best-performing sites under the selected criteria. LunaNav also supports custom coordinates and clearly indicates when data are unavailable or when a conclusion cannot be recommended.

The project separates published source data from calculations performed by LunaNav, including rankings and weighted scores. It also communicates important limitations, such as the distinction between Earth visibility and guaranteed communication and the fact that some environmental factors are not used to produce a recommendation.

LunaNav was developed as a transparent, accessible prototype to make complex lunar data easier to explore and use in early mission-planning concepts. It is designed to support clearer comparisons rather than replace detailed scientific or engineering analysis.

Tools used include a web-based application development platform, Canva for presentation and visual materials, and AI assistance for ideation, coding/debugging, and writing or translation.
